## Who may do what

For each action, the combinations `sekisho check` walked, put together where Cedar answers them alike and the same policies decide. Rows that differ in one column only are one row, the column holding their values: `any` is every value the column takes, `not …` every value but one. `-` is a column that does not apply to the row (the roles of a workflow, say).

## Policies

Each policy as the `.gate` writes it, beside the Cedar `sekisho gen --target cedar` generates for it. A permit allows the combinations it applies to; a forbid denies those it applies to, and wins where a permit applies too. Cedar denies a combination no policy applies to. A condition on a rule's answer names the value as the `.rule` writes it (`within_limit`) in the `.gate`, and as the string Cedar is given (`"within_limit"`) in the Cedar.

### permit `staff_view_purchases`

The staff look at any purchase

- On `view_purchase`, it allows 3 combinations, and no other permit allows any of them.

`approvals.gate`

```gate
permit staff_view_purchases
  description "The staff look at any purchase"
  principal in employee
  action view_purchase
```

`cedar/approvals.cedar`

```cedar
@id("approvals/staff_view_purchases")
@doc("The staff look at any purchase")
permit (
  principal in Office::Role::"employee",
  action == Office::Action::"view_purchase",
  resource is Office::Purchase
);
```

### permit `approvers_approve_within_their_limit`

An approver approves a submitted purchase someone else asked for, up to the approver's own limit

- On `approve`, it allows 2 combinations, and no other permit allows any of them.

`approvals.gate`

```gate
permit approvers_approve_within_their_limit
  description "An approver approves a submitted purchase someone else asked for, up to the approver's own limit"
  principal in approver
  action approve
  when resource.status is submitted
  when band is within_limit
  unless resource.requester is principal
```

`cedar/approvals.cedar`

```cedar
@id("approvals/approvers_approve_within_their_limit")
@doc("An approver approves a submitted purchase someone else asked for, up to the approver's own limit")
permit (
  principal in Office::Role::"approver",
  action == Office::Action::"approve",
  resource is Office::Purchase
)
when { resource.status == "submitted" }
when { context.band == "within_limit" }
unless { resource.requester == principal };
```

### permit `approvers_ask_for_what_they_cannot_approve`

An approver asks a higher approver to approve a submitted purchase, only when the approver could not approve it

- On `request_approval`, it allows 6 combinations, and no other permit allows any of them.

`approvals.gate`

```gate
permit approvers_ask_for_what_they_cannot_approve
  description "An approver asks a higher approver to approve a submitted purchase, only when the approver could not approve it"
  principal in approver
  action request_approval
  when resource.status is submitted
  unless allowed approve
```

`cedar/approvals.cedar`

```cedar
@id("approvals/approvers_ask_for_what_they_cannot_approve")
@doc("An approver asks a higher approver to approve a submitted purchase, only when the approver could not approve it")
permit (
  principal in Office::Role::"approver",
  action == Office::Action::"request_approval",
  resource is Office::Purchase
)
when { resource.status == "submitted" }
unless { context.allowed_approve };
```

## Computed values

What an action computes and gives Cedar in its context. The generated code computes each one from the service's own data, the operation's arguments and the server's clock, and never takes it from the caller. The pages of the rules and the dates are the pages for people that rulec and koyomi draw, as they draw them.

### `band` of `approve`

- Written: `band = approval_limit(amount: amount, limit: principal.approval_limit).band`
- Computed by `rulec "rules/approval_limit.rule" output band`, from `amount` and `principal.approval_limit`.
- Its values: `within_limit` and `over_limit`; Cedar is given the strings `"within_limit"` and `"over_limit"`.

### `band` of `request_approval`

- Written: `band = approval_limit(amount: amount, limit: principal.approval_limit).band`
- Computed by `rulec "rules/approval_limit.rule" output band`, from `amount` and `principal.approval_limit`.
- Its values: `within_limit` and `over_limit`; Cedar is given the strings `"within_limit"` and `"over_limit"`.

The page of this file is under `band` above.

### `allowed_approve` of `request_approval`

- Written: `allowed approve(amount: amount)`
- Whether `approve` is allowed for the same principal and resource, on the same day. The generated code asks it first, through the function of `approve`, and puts the answer in the context before it asks this action; why `approve` was refused, when it was, is why this request is refused.
- What the inputs of `approve` are given: `amount` ← `amount`.
- Its values: yes and no (true and false in Cedar).
- Its values are as the table of `approve` on this page says.

## Expectations, separations and roles

### Expectations

- `no_one_asks_for_what_they_could_approve` (expects deny, on `request_approval`): No one asks for an approval of a purchase they could approve themselves. It holds on all 2 combinations it picks.
- `approvers_ask_over_their_limit` (expects allow, on `request_approval`): An approver asks for an approval of a submitted purchase over the approver's own limit. It holds on all 4 combinations it picks.
- `approvers_ask_for_their_own_purchases` (expects allow, on `request_approval`): An approver asks for an approval of a submitted purchase the approver asked for, which no one approves for themselves. It holds on all 4 combinations it picks.
- `only_approvers_approve_or_ask_for_approvals` (expects deny, on `approve`, `request_approval`): An employee who is not an approver neither approves a purchase nor asks for an approval. It holds on all 32 combinations it picks.

### Roles

- `employee`: Asks for what the work needs, and looks at the purchases. Its `can` lists `view_purchase`.
- `approver`: Approves the purchases others ask for, up to an approver's own limit. It includes `employee`. Its `can` lists `view_purchase`, `approve` and `request_approval`.

Whether a principal holding one role alone (and the roles it includes) is allowed each action: always, in every combination of the rest; sometimes, allowed in some combinations and denied in others; never, denied in every one. `-` is an action that does not take the principal's type. Where a role writes `can`, `sekisho check` holds the actions it is always or sometimes allowed to it.

| principal | `view_purchase` | `approve` | `request_approval` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `User` holding `employee` | always | never | never |
| `User` holding `approver` | always | sometimes | sometimes |

## Operations guarded

No action guards an operation of a contract.
